description:
**Divergence**: every extension-server sibling carries an AGENTS.md with the canonical-template banner. Almost no extension-types or extension-client sibling does.

**Missing per-crate AGENTS.md** (extension siblings only, ignoring testjig which is publish=false):
- chat-client
- calendars-client, calendars-types
- tasks-client, tasks-types
- contacts-client, contacts-types
- filenode-client, filenode-types
- sharing-client, sharing-types
- metadata-client, metadata-types

**Have one** (canonical and the only-sibling-with-banner):
- All 8 extension-server crates (mail-server canonical + 7 siblings with 'Sibling of the canonical jmap-mail-server' banner block at lines 3-21)
- mail-types and mail-client (canonical extension-types and extension-client templates)
- chat-types (sibling; acknowledges canonical at lines 12-16; also self-canonical for the JMAP Chat draft)

**Caller-observable / maintainer effect**: the workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' rule says 'when you change a non-canonical sibling and the change diverges from the canonical template, the rule is: change the canonical first, then propagate' and 'Each canonical crate's AGENTS.md carries a short canonical-template banner reminding contributors of the propagation rule'. A contributor (or agent) opening calendars-types or filenode-client without a per-crate AGENTS.md has no in-tree reminder that the crate is bound to a canonical template. The propagation rule is meaningless against a sibling that has no AGENTS.md to carry the 'mirror this one' acknowledgement.

**Asymmetry is striking**: extension-server crates (which already have heavyweight backend traits and the most complex public surface) are uniformly well-templated. Extension-types and extension-client crates (which have simpler surfaces but where the workspace's cookie-cutter consistency matters MORE because there are more analogous types to keep aligned) are uniformly under-templated. The opposite of the priority that the propagation rule suggests.

**Fix**: cookie-cut a per-crate AGENTS.md into each of the 13 missing siblings, modeled on the 7 server-sibling banners. The clean reference is crate-jmap-tasks-server/AGENTS.md:3-21. The acknowledgement template is roughly:

  ## 🧬 Sibling of the canonical {jmap-mail-types | jmap-mail-client}
  
  Every change that touches this crate's public-API shape, test layout, or convention
  must either come FROM a corresponding change to the canonical, or come WITH a
  follow-up sweep bead to propagate to the canonical and the other 6 siblings.
  Differences from the canonical are differences mandated by the relevant RFC,
  draft, or this crate's role in the dep graph — nothing else.

**Recommended priority**: P2. Not blocking any specific bug but progressively undermines the rule's enforceability with every new sibling change.

**Cross-references**: JMAP-76wm (README convention sweep — similar workspace-wide consistency epic; was the prior pass that converged all 32 crates onto the six-section README shape).
title: Workspace: 15 of 32 crates lack a per-crate AGENTS.md — propagation rule cannot apply against missing files (extension-types and extension-client siblings)
